title: ROAS Calculator
description: Measure advertising revenue for every unit of ad spend.
body:
Calculate return on ad spend (ROAS) to understand how much revenue your advertising generates. Use revenue attributed to the same campaign and period as your spend.

How to calculate ROAS

Divide attributed revenue by advertising spend. For example, 5,000 in revenue ÷ 1,000 in spend = 5× ROAS, or 500%.

Use the same currency for both inputs. ROAS measures revenue efficiency; it does not account for product costs, overhead, or net profit.

title: Profit Margin Calculator
description: See your profit and margin before making the next move.
body:
Calculate profit and profit margin from your revenue and total costs. Include the costs relevant to your decision, such as products, shipping, platform fees, and advertising.

How to calculate profit margin

Profit = revenue − cost. Profit margin = profit ÷ revenue × 100. For example, 100 revenue and 60 cost gives 40 profit and a 40% margin.

Use the same currency and period for both inputs. Costs above revenue produce a negative margin. Margin is different from markup, which divides profit by cost.

title: Print DPI Calculator
description: Check image resolution at your intended print size.
body:
Estimate horizontal and vertical image resolution from pixel dimensions and physical print size. This is pixels per inch (PPI), commonly called print DPI. It does not measure a printer’s ink dots.

How to calculate print resolution

Divide each pixel dimension by its print dimension in inches. For example, 3,000 × 2,400 pixels printed at 10 × 8 inches gives 300 PPI on both axes. Centimeters are converted using 2.54 cm per inch.

Around 300 PPI is a common starting point for close-viewed prints; requirements depend on the printer, material, and viewing distance. Different horizontal and vertical values may indicate an aspect-ratio mismatch. Confirm cropping or stretching with your printer.
